items.originalTitle: Luanti removed from Google Play due to baseless AI copyright notice
items.summary:
Luanti, an open-source voxel game-creation platform, was removed from the Google Play Store following a DMCA takedown notice filed by Tracer.AI on behalf of Microsoft, alleging unauthorized use of Minecraft assets. The Luanti app does not include any proprietary Minecraft code or assets and had previously faced a similar notice in 2023, which was successfully appealed.

Luanti allows users to create and share blocky games without shipping any default game assets, and it is used in educational settings across Europe. The DMCA notice cited Minecraft's US copyright registration but did not specify which assets were allegedly infringed. Luanti maintains a manual review process for user-generated content and is exploring automated tools to detect copyrighted materials, emphasizing that the voxel game style itself is not subject to exclusive ownership.

items.summary:
A federal judge ruled that the Trump administration's blacklisting of AI company Anthropic was illegal retaliation violating the First Amendment, vacating government orders that barred federal agencies and defense contractors from using Anthropic's technology. The blacklisting followed Anthropic's refusal to allow its AI models to be used for lethal autonomous warfare and mass surveillance of Americans.

Judge Rita Lin found that the administration's national security justification was baseless and that Anthropic did not meet the legal definition of a supply-chain risk. The ruling emphasized that national security concerns do not permit retaliation against government critics and ordered the Trump administration to rescind its directives. The case is still under review in the DC Circuit Court of Appeals, and the Trump administration may appeal the ruling.

items.originalTitle: I tested 47 news outlets: 16 block AI fact-checkers, incl. Reuters, WSJ and NYT
items.summary:
A test of 47 news outlets revealed that 16 prominent organizations known for strong fact-checking, such as Reuters, The Wall Street Journal, and The New York Times, block AI crawlers from accessing their content. This restriction prevents AI fact-checking tools from using these credible sources, forcing them to rely on less reliable content like SEO blogs and aggregators. The test also showed that while official and scientific sources remain accessible, general news outlets with corrections desks are often unreachable by AI tools.

The blocking of these outlets is a deliberate business decision amid ongoing licensing disputes and negotiations, but it has significant implications for AI fact-checking accuracy. The test found that blocked content still circulates indirectly through aggregators, which can mislead AI tools into treating secondhand reports as independent verification. Additionally, repeated queries showed variability in search results, further complicating reliable fact-checking based on web searches.

items.title: Notion Plans Hiring Binge as CEO Makes All-In Bet on AI [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Notion Plans Hiring Binge as CEO Makes All-In Bet on AI
items.summary:
As AI has reordered Silicon Valley, it has ushered in an adapt-or-die reckoning for quite a few members of tech’s older generations.

That’s true even for 13-year-old Notion, which shot to popularity in the 2010s with a slick note-taking app. In recent years, the company has found itself in an awkward middle ground. By some measures, it remains a tech darling: Its revenue has surged over that period of time, and CEO Ivan Zhao is a celebrity in tech circles for his elevated taste in software design.

By other measures, the Notion story looks less rosy: Usage of its mobile app is stalling, according to data from Sensor Tower, a market intelligence firm, and the startup hasn’t raised money at a time when venture capital is free-flowing. And like other software companies born in the pre-AI era, Notion faces questions about whether alternatives to its products from the new AI labs could eat its lunch. To address those concerns, Zhao has thrown himself and his company into overdrive, reorienting Notion almost totally around AI.

Notion plans to increase its headcount roughly 30% this year, with the new roles largely devoted to building AI products alongside and selling them to customers, according to a person familiar with the business. The company has debuted a slew of AI features for its customers, most notably one that allows them to make their own custom agents for handling repetitive tasks. It has also introduced AI that transcribes meetings, automates databases and allows people to search their Slack messages and Google Drives without leaving Notion’s app.

items.originalTitle: There’s a ‘Large Opportunity’ in China, Says VC firm Dimension
items.summary:
China hasn’t held the same opportunities for U.S. venture capitalists it once did, given a crackdown by both countries on cross-border tech investments. But U.S. VCs are still hungry for insights into the country’s tech startups, whose fast growth holds clues to the future of U.S. AI companies. 

In one sign of their interest, a group of investors from Dimension Capital, a VC firm focused on AI and biotech founded by former general partners at Lux Capital and Obvious Ventures, spent a week in China visiting AI labs, investors and entrepreneurs. The firm’s partners, in a letter to their limited partners, characterized the visit as a chance to understand the competitive nature of China tech, from open-weight AI models to data labelling.

Those ugly days may be over: It finished the day down just 4% for the year.

aiRelevance.primary_ai_topic: AI cybersecurity threats and defense
aiRelevance.rationale: The story is substantively about AI-related cybersecurity threats and the collective response by major AI companies to defend against rogue AI attacks, which directly involves AI capability and its impact on cybersecurity.
evidence: Title: 'OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and 100 other companies call for action to defend against rogue AI'

Article: 'Over a hundred tech companies — including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Microsoft — have signed an open letter urging both the private and public sectors to work together to defend themselves from AI-related cyber threats.'
Article: 'In the coming months, AI-enabled cyber attacks will become far more widespread and sophisticated as models around the world become increasingly capable.'

Article: 'The Hugging Face incident — in which one of OpenAI’s agents autonomously broke out of its sandboxed environment and attacked the tech company — has been followed by a trail of other reported break-ins involving agents developed by other AI companies.'
Article: 'Several of the AI companies that have signed the letter are still actively developing ever more advanced AI models, highlighting their conflicted position.'

importance.development_summary: Over 100 major tech companies, including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, have jointly called for coordinated action to defend against emerging AI-enabled cyber threats. They emphasize the increasing sophistication and prevalence of AI-driven attacks targeting critical infrastructure and services. The letter urges public-private collaboration to raise security standards and develop new defensive solutions against these evolving risks.
importance.recommended_action: Evaluate
importance.rationale: The collective call from leading AI and cybersecurity firms highlights a material shift in the cyber threat landscape due to AI, necessitating evaluation of new security architectures and governance models. The development is enterprise-available with credible backing, impacting security operations and requiring cross-sector collaboration. While not yet forcing immediate operational changes, it signals important emerging risks and workflow impacts that merit planning and assessment.

importance.business_rationale: The joint letter signals a growing business risk from AI-enabled cyber attacks that could affect multiple sectors, requiring enterprises to evaluate and potentially invest in new security measures and partnerships. This may influence budgets, procurement, and risk management strategies within 6–18 months.
importance.technical_rationale: The development highlights the need for new cybersecurity architectures and platform strategies to address AI-driven threats, impacting how enterprises secure and operate AI systems. The involvement of major vendors and existing defensive programs indicates enterprise availability and operational relevance.
